translation_notes: sh = rdflib.Namespace(...) becomes '@prefix sh: <...> as SH .': the 'as SH' binding is needed because the function also uses sh.ignoredProperties/sh["in"] as ordinary Python values (loop targets, .subject_objects(pred) arguments), not just in term position.
graph.remove((None, sh.order, None)) -> '-{ ?s sh:order ?o }' (unbound variable = wildcard, matches the 'remove' stratum).

graph.remove((subject, pred, head)) -> '-{ {subject} {pred} {head} }': all three positions are fully bound Python values here (not a wildcard pattern), so this stays a precise single-triple removal, unlike the neighbouring wildcard remove above.

graph.add((subject, pred, new_head)) -> '+{ {subject} {pred} {new_head} }' under a single '@graph graph' designated once at the top of the function (graph is never reassigned, so one designation covers the whole body).

_blank_node_labels is a sibling top-level function in the source file, not visible in the extracted region/context: restored via context_shim.py (verbatim from the source repo) per AGENT_BATCH.md's context-shim convention.

The entry point takes turtle_text: str and parses its own graph, so the driver reads fixture.ttl as text and passes it directly via calls=[...] rather than through run_pair's fixture= (which would hand it a pre-parsed Graph object).
optimization_notes: optimized.py: Graph().parse(...) chained (parse returns the graph); the list items are sorted when read (`sorted(Collection(...), key=str)`) instead of listed then sorted at rebuild; the fallback branch inlines emit and replaces the `if line` generator with filter(None, ...); term() loses the redundant str() around n3() and its intermediate name; the header list is inlined into the join with `*lines`. The per-triple remove/add are kept: graph.set would drop a second list hanging from the same subject and predicate.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `@prefix sh:` without `as SH`, since `(sh:ignoredProperties, sh:in)` are prefixed names in a Python tuple; `@graph as graph` then graph.parse(...); the wildcard remove becomes `-{ ?s sh:order ?o }`, the per-list remove and add `-{ }` and `+{ }`; graph.subject_objects(pred) becomes `m{ ?subject {pred} ?head }`. Collection and rdflib.BNode() stay: no island builds an RDF list in place or mints an anonymous fresh blank node outside g{ }.

The driver's fixture only exercises the forest path; the to_canonical_graph fallback was checked by hand on a non-forest input (a blank node with two incoming edges, an empty and a two-element sh:in on one subject): original, optimized.py and optimized.ldpy return the same text.
header_optimization_notes: Nothing unused in the header on either side (typing.Any and the _blank_node_labels shim are both used; the prefix is declared inside the function): optimized_header.py and optimized_header.ldpy are copies of the optimized artefacts.
